messages:
ellie_customer: Hey team — our service in the customer's VPC started failing to establish mTLS to the Redwood Private control plane this morning. App logs show 'SSL alert number 40' / 'handshake_failure'. Happening from a subset of hosts behind our corp egress proxy. Can you help?

mike_support: @ellie_customer thanks — can you paste the exact command you used and any openssl / curl output? Also which control plane endpoint IP are you hitting?

ellie_customer: Using our normal client certs, example run:
```
openssl s_client -connect control.redwood-private.example:443 -cert client.pem -key client.key -showcerts
CONNECTED(00000003)
140736893469952:error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert handshake failure:../ssl/record/rec_layer_s3.c:1524:SSL alert number 40
```

devon_sre: Can you capture a tcpdump of the 3rd-party egress hop (port 443) while reproducing? Looking for ClientHello/SNI and whether something in the middle is terminating TLS.

ellie_customer: Paste of tcpdump excerpt (sanitized):
```
09:31:12.123456 IP 10.1.2.3.54321 > 52.149.12.8.443: Flags [S], seq 0
09:31:12.223456 IP 10.1.2.3.54321 > 52.149.12.8.443: ClientHello (len=512) SNI: control.redwood-private.example
09:31:12.225600 IP 10.1.2.1.44444 > 10.1.2.3.54321: TLS-Inspect-Agent "BlueProxy v6" accepted connection
09:31:12.226000 IP 52.149.12.8.443 > 10.1.2.1.44444: RST
```

tara_netops: That middlebox line looks telling — our corporate TLS inspection is terminating the ClientHello and attempting to re-initiate TLS to the control plane without forwarding the original client cert. For mutual TLS we need true TCP passthrough so the client cert reaches our control plane.

mike_support: Confirming: because the proxy is doing TLS MITM, it strips the client cert and/or injects its own cert chain, so the control plane never sees the client identity -> handshake fails. Action item: ask customer to exempt the control plane IP/CIDR from TLS inspection / SSL proxy and configure passthrough for ports 443 (and any custom port like 8443). Also ensure SNI/ALPN are passed through unchanged.

ellie_customer: We applied an exemption for 52.149.12.0/24 and set the TLS proxy to TCP passthrough for that CIDR. Re-ran the same openssl command:
```
openssl s_client -connect control.redwood-private.example:443 -cert client.pem -key client.key -showcerts
CONNECTED(00000003)
SSL-Session:
    Protocol  : TLSv1.3
    Cipher    : TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
Verify return code: 0 (ok)
```

devon_sre: Excellent — that confirms the proxy was the cause. Two follow-ups: 1) customer should avoid adding our control plane to any device-level trust stores (that doesn't help for mTLS) and 2) we should add a KB entry describing corporate TLS inspection breakage and the exact control plane CIDRs/SNI to exempt.

mike_support: I'll draft the KB and update the private deployment onboarding checklist to include "exempt control plane IPs from TLS inspection (do not terminate mTLS)" + sample tcpdump/openssl commands for customers to validate. :white_check_mark:

inc_bot: Ticket SUP-4321 marked resolved by mike_support

mike_support: Closing the thread after customer confirmed. If anyone sees similar issues, check for TLS interception first (tcpdump showing proxy identifier) before digging into certs or cipher suites.
